response: Yes, infants discharged from a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) are at a higher risk for health problems if exposed to secondhand smoke, and this exposure can exacerbate existing health disparities. Secondhand smoke exposure can increase the risk of respiratory problems, such as bronchiolitis and asthma, as well as sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) and other health issues. Infants from low-income families or minority groups may be more likely to be exposed to secondhand smoke due to higher smoking rates among their caregivers and less access to smoke-free environments, thereby widening health disparities.
